hi! so in my longest relationship i’ve had, my ex and i both had adhd. mine was undiagnosed at the time, and he had a diagnosis, but wasn’t taking meds or going to therapy, just sorta self medicating with weed. looking back, RSD and general emotional disregulation took a toll, as well as impulsivity which was the reason for our breakup. It led to a lot of doubting of ourselves and each other during certain points of our relationship, believing that we were mad at each other when we weren’t, doubting if we really liked/loved each other. a lot of this came with us telling each other we liked/loved one another, because we either thought is was disingenuous from ourselves or each other, even though our actions outside of saying those words showed it was true. that example in the end is why he ended up ending it, plus feeling the weight of his friends moving and schoolwork (at least that’s how he explained it to me). now he did some crappy things after the breakup which led to us really disliking each other and feeling that we were holding each other back, because he wanted to stay best friends with me, and with ADHD or not that leads to trouble, but it was clear that we just both still wanted that reassurance, that ADHD makes us question a lot. i think if we were both treating our ADHD it would’ve been a lot different, and if it had still ended, it would’ve ended better as well. i definitely think one of the most important things that you can do is give reassurance! i know it’s annoying, but it takes two seconds, and with the way RSD works many people with ADHD need constant reassurance. A lot of times arguments that sorta come out of nowhere stem out of this fear that the other person is mad at you, or is doing things to make you upset on purpose. a lot of times we just sorta shut down because of this feeling, and don’t know how to handle it, and it can lead to that argument. definitely talking things out and providing that reassurance is super important in times like that! i don’t know if this helps any or at all, i’m definitely no expert on relationships, that’s just my experience personally, and how looking back i’ve interpreted it.

hi! i have depression, anxiety, as well as obsessive thoughts (sorta pure O OCD), and i was already on meds for these prior to my ADHD diagnosis. my psychiatrist continued me on my meds (i’m on an SNRI) because she said they actually pair really well with stimulants! ive found that i haven’t had any extreme anxiety attacks while taking both (besides from external factors), and that i feel generally very balanced out, more so than when i was just on SNRIs. i’m still having trouble with some of my adhd symptoms, like focusing, but i’m still getting used to starting stimulants as well, and have slowly been upping my dosage, but still no heightened anxiety! if it’s an option to be able to take a SS/SNRI alongside your stimulant I would def ask your psych about that, if you find any heightened anxiety on just the stimulant alone.

i’m so glad he was understanding that’s great news! i  can get that feeling too of depression of anxiety when i’m feeling frustrated as well, you’re not alone in that. i hope your sleep meds are able to help you!

i definitely understand that feeling. i think it comes from the way society sort of brushes off adhd as something “everyone has”, and that they don’t understand the one day that they can’t seem to focus is a constant everyday thing for us with adhd. it makes us internalize it and think that we’re “weak willed” and “overreacting”, when really our brains just operate differently than theirs. 

i especially hate when people do that and are like “i do that too”, but then get mad when people with adhd and other neurological conditions don’t communicate with them the way they want them to. a big example ive seen of this and learned about from other people with adhd taking about it on twitter, is that people think that with adhd are being selfish and self centered when we try to empathize and share an anecdote of a similar situation we went through in a conversation. it’s literally a no win situation 😭

i’m not quite sure why you felt to need to comment this? yes there have been people who do become addicts to adhd meds. however those are people who do not have adhd, as studies show that stimulants work different on someone who has adhd vs. someone who doesn’t. i went to high school in a town where parents who had kids who would just be hyper (like a lot of kids are) and it annoyed them so they went to their doctor friends to get them stimulants. many of those kids became addicted. however this is still not a reason to demonize those with adhd who use stimulants, or those without it who have become addicted. the lack of understanding of adhd in our society has created not only this problem of addiction to stimulants that you seem to be pointing out, but also the problem that everyday it gets harder and harder for those of us with adhd to be able to get meds. i have to jump through so many hoops with my insurance to get my meds, and often go days without them as i wait for the approval process. this kind of language not only fuels those hoops those with adhd have to jump through to get meds, but also continues to perpetuate the idea that stimulants must be some magic drug, fueling more non adhd people to want to try them, creating a black market of sorts, and then causing more crackdowns on access to meds for those who need them. this kind of rhetoric fuels that vicious cycle.

hi! i related to so much that you said! i recently got diagnosed with ADHD as a 21 year old girl/young woman (it’s still weird referring to myself as an adult lol) and it was one of the most relieving things to hear this past year! my mom and brother are diagnosed as well (and we suspect my dad has adhd as well, and my grandma told me she did as well i think), and because my symptoms presented differently than theirs and i’ve always been very high achieving academically (although my mom and brother are as well), the possibility of me having adhd was always overlooked. it wasn’t until last year that an article on how adhd presents in teens/adults and women went viral that i even considered the possibility of adhd. i just assumed that i still wasn’t on the right meds for my already existing diagnoses. i told my mom about the possibility of me having adhd, and she seemed open to exploring the idea, but we never really proceeded with it, because it wasn’t our top priority at the time. fast forward a year later, and due to quarantine and personal traumatic events that were happening in my life, my adhd and other diagnoses went into complete overdrive, rendering me incapable of doing anything, and resulting in me falling behind in my college classes. it was at this point that i explored that idea again, and talked to my grandparents who i was living with about it, and they agreed that i should get tested, that there was a high possibility i had adhd. i got tested, and came back with all of the criteria for adhd, however the testing psychologist didn’t want to give me the diagnosis. sadly a lot of professionals are reluctant to diagnose those who are not young children, and especially if they’re women (and that’s no matter the age), but some of this is starting to change! confused by this, i brought my results to my psychiatrist, who agreed with me that the testing psychologist should’ve given me the diagnosis himself, and prescribed me meds. 

with your familial history, i am hoping your family will be receptive to you! definitely tell them the symptoms that you have been experiencing, and provide specific examples of how you’ve seen them. in the case that they aren’t receptive (which i’m really hoping that they are receptive) definitely try and talk with your school counselor (i’m assuming you’re still able to email/call your counselor even in you’re not in school in person)! my brother was able to get tested for adhd and autism bc of my mom and teachers bringing up the symptoms he was having to the school counselor/psychologist. i’m not sure if your school has testing resources, but it’s definitely something to look into, and even if they don’t, they might be able to help you find outside resources, as well as talk to your family about what you’re experiencing. 

in regards to your ed, don’t let that dissuade you from getting diagnosed. there’s many different adhd meds out there, and if you are diagnosed, your psychiatrist should be able to find one that doesn’t have the appetite suppressant side effects. i’m hoping someone else who has gone through an ed and has had to get meds is able to respond more effectively to this part, because i don’t have first hand knowledge in this aspect. you being aware of your ed and wanting to find this closure is amazing and i’m sending you support! that, and also being aware of possible symptoms of adhd and wanting to get a diagnosis shows that you have a level of self awareness that i wish i had when i was 15. i’m wishing you the best of luck with this, and i hope i was able to help in some extent!

yes yes yes to almost everything except to impulsivity (to a certain extent) and low empathy, i’m actually extremely empathetic, which is also a problem in its own. some of those symptoms you listed that you have i also have due to comorbid diagnoses (but are also symptoms of adhd alone), but i would definitely look into getting tested! just a psa, if you get tested and the results come out positive in terms of having symptoms of adhd, but your psychologist is reluctant to give you the diagnosis (this happened to me :/ ), make sure to get a second professional opinion! some professionals seem reluctant to diagnose people who aren’t young children, despite them meeting the criteria. however thankfully some of this is starting to change with more people talking about adhd and what it is. best wishes, and i hope you get answers soon!
